title: I Used the Mbira-Key Hours on the Lead Who Palmed My Numbered Buzzers

parts.text: I stepped into the gourd room at 4:04 p.m. and lead Tendai was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE MBIRA. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. BUZZERS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered buzzers. Tendai shrugged. "Leads are the keys." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover bottle caps on my numbered buzzers. Then I asked for the buzzer log. At 4:12 the desk pinged why Tendai's name was on my caps. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Tendai's leftover bottle caps on my numbered buzzers.

social.video_title: He palmed my numbered mbira buzzers on my hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Gourd room, leftover bottle caps, a forty-five-minute clock he posted. I logged the buzzers. Would you have asked for the buzzer log?

parts.text: Tendai called it buzz dressing until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the cap still. The buzzers went back to my numbered slot. Tendai ran a slot of his own and told the next lead atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE KEYS. I keep my buzzers in a labeled tin. Tendai brown-bags his dressing. The gourd room finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Leads are not the keys — Part 2/2
social.description: Buzzer log, numbered buzzers, and a second line on the board. Was buzz dressing ever my caps?
